title: Audit ingestion & retention strategy for RBAC v2 / SSO event stream
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Design and deliver a scalable, cost-controlled audit ingestion pipeline and storage lifecycle for RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML administrative events. This must satisfy compliance retention SLAs, support forensic queries (per-tenant, per-user, time-window), and enable efficient day-to-day debugging and rollout analysis for admin controls.

Background & constraints:
- RBAC v2 introduces richer policy primitives and more frequent admin events (policy create/update/delete, role bindings, permission evals). SSO/SAML login/link events are high-cardinality and often heavy during org migrations.
- We must avoid unbounded storage growth and keep egress/query costs predictable.
- Logs must be tamper-evident, encrypted at rest, and indexed for search and analytics. PII must be scrubbed at ingestion unless explicitly required and approved.
- Phase 1 must work for hosted and Dedicated customers; Private deployments will use same schema and ILM guidance but may have different transport.

Requirements:
- Schema: canonical audit event with fields: timestamp, tenant_id, actor_id, actor_type, resource_type, resource_id, action, outcome, before_hash, after_hash, request_id, trace_id, service, event_source, event_version. Schema evolution path and versioning must be supported.
- Durability: SLA of 99.9% ingestion availability; bounded ingestion latency (95th <= 2s under normal load).
- Retention: default 90 days hot searchable; archival to cold object storage (S3) at 90d, with legal hold option up to 7 years.
- Query patterns: recent forensic searches (last 30d) by tenant/user/action; aggregated rollups for cost dashboards; long-term policy-change timelines via compacted events.
- Security: all audit data encrypted with KMS, write-audit trail for schema changes, HMAC/append-only markers for tamper evidence.

Proposed architecture (phase 1):
1) Ingestion: events emitted from services via buffered HTTPS to an ingress fleet (Nginx + Envoy) -> validated and enriched by Audit Ingest API (go) -> written to Kafka topic for durability. Use idempotency keys (request_id). Backpressure: Kafka partitions per-tenant-shard to ensure isolation for hot tenants.
2) Real-time processing: Consumer group runs small stateless processors to validate schema, scrub PII (config-driven), add tenant routing metadata, and write to two sinks: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch 'hot' index and S3 raw events.
3) Hot storage: Time-based indices in OpenSearch with ILM policies (rollover every 50GB or daily). Index naming: audit-yyyy.MM.dd-tenantshard. Primary index keys include tenant_id + event_type for shard affinity. Use doc_values and keyword mappings only for fields required for filter. Keep full message stored in _source for first 30 days, then move to metadata-only indexes.
4) Cold storage: S3 compressed parquet/ndjson with partitioning by year/month/tenant. An indexer runs to build compacted slices for long-term timeline queries; also keep a minimal metadata index for fast existence checks.
5) Retention & lifecycle: ILM to force rollover -> after 30d, downsample full_text to metadata-only index, after 90d move source to S3 and delete heavy indices. Legal hold and export endpoints to pin data.
6) Cost controls: tiered indices (hot/warm/cold), doc-level TTL for high-volume noisy event types, automatic downsampling (1/min summaries) for telemetry, retention quotas per customer configurable on Dedicated.

Indexing & partitioning decisions (trade-offs):
- Partition key: date + tenant_shard + event_type. Rationale: balances time-range queries and tenant isolation; reduces shard explosion by using tenant_shard rather than full tenant_id.
- Use daily rollovers with size threshold instead of hourly to limit number of shards.
- Keep high-cardinality fields (actor_id, request_id) as keyword but avoid indexing full JSON blobs to control index size.

Operational controls:
- Backfill/repair: consumer idempotency + dedupe by request_id; reindexer tool for schema upgrades.
- Monitoring: ingestion lag dashboards, partition imbalance alerts, missing-event detectors (alerts when expected event rate drops >50% for 5m), cost burn-rate alarms per tenant.
- On-call playbooks: steps for slow consumers, broker partition rebalancing, and emergency retention override.

Privacy & compliance:
- Default PII redaction rules (email, SSN patterns) at ingest with allow-list for approved investigations. Access to raw events requires elevated role and is logged.
- Audit logs of the audit-system itself must be stored in separate append-only path and encrypted with separate KMS key.

Open questions / trade-offs for review:
- Hot index retention: 30d vs 90d by default (cost vs convenience). Recommendation: 30d default, opt-up to 90d for customers on enterprise retention.
- Compression/codecs: use best compression supported by OpenSearch vs storing pre-compressed parquet in S3.
- Tamper-evidence: HMAC chain vs ledger-style append-only store (bookkeeping complexity).

Deliverables & timeline:
- Week 1 (Spike): PoC Kafka-backed ingest + small OpenSearch index (ENG spike).
- Week 2-3: PII scrubber lib + schema registry + enrichment service.
- Week 4: ILM policies, rollover, and downsampling pipeline.
- Week 5: S3 archival worker and restore flow.
- Week 6: Dashboards + alerts + runbook + security review.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingest pipeline can sustain 10k events/sec sustained in staging with <2s 95th latency.
- Query latency for hot indices: 95th < 300ms for typical filters.
- End-to-end retention policy moving old indices to S3 and removing heavy indices validated in staging.
- Security review completed and tamper-evidence mechanism validated.

Notes: coordinate with infra (ENG-9478) for Kafka capacity and with Console team for query APIs (ENG-9563).
acceptance_criteria: Staging ingest at 10k events/sec with 95th percentile <2s
Hot index queries (filters by tenant_id + action) 95th <300ms
ILM moves indices to cold storage at 90d and S3 archive restored successfully in test
PII redaction verified and privileged access audit works
Tamper-evidence proof-of-concept validated by security review
